title: Vaineau, Barachant & Andreev 2013 — Brain Invaders Adaptive versus Non-Adaptive P300 Brain-Computer Interface dataset (BI2013a)
description: EEG recordings from 24 healthy participants performing a visual P300 Brain-Computer Interface task based on the Brain Invaders video game. The experiment compared a P300 BCI with and without adaptive calibration using Riemannian geometry, with adaptive and non-adaptive runs in randomised order across eight sessions per subject. Data were acquired with 16 wet electrodes at 512 Hz at GIPSA-lab, Grenoble, in 2013.
methods_description: Sixteen-channel EEG was recorded with a g.USBamp amplifier (g.tec) at 512 Hz, referenced to the left earlobe, using OpenViBE. Each session had two runs (Non-Adaptive and Adaptive, randomised), each with a Training (calibration) phase of 80 Target and 400 non-Target flashes and an Online phase of variable length. The Brain Invaders interface presented 36 symbols in 12 groups. Participants were blind to the mode of operation.
